name: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
problem: LLM applications increasingly need MULTIPLE generation calls, control flow, advanced prompting, and structured input/output - but efficient systems for programming and executing such programs did not exist. Naive multi-turn and multi-call patterns waste prefill on re-reading an unchanged prefix.
mechanism: A frontend language plus a runtime. Frontend provides primitives for generation and explicit parallelism control, so programs are not implicitly sequential. Runtime contributes two optimisations that matter for this slice: RADIXATTENTION, which organises the KV cache in a radix tree over token sequences so a shared prefix across calls is matched and reused rather than recomputed (this is the prefix-reuse mechanism behind agentic multi-turn serving), and COMPRESSED FINITE STATE MACHINES for faster structured-output decoding, which collapses grammar/constraint automaton states into a compact representation so the per-token mask computation on the critical path is cheaper.
speedup_reported: Up to 6.4x higher throughput than state-of-the-art inference systems, across various large language and multimodal models, on tasks INCLUDING agent control, logical reasoning, few-shot learning, JSON decoding, retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, and multi-turn chat. The headline is a THROUGHPUT number against a baseline serving system, on a program-level workload - not a batch-1 latency multiplier, which makes it directly relevant to this repo's benchmark records rather than only comparable to other systems papers.
notes:
ADOPTION: SGLang itself is a production-grade serving engine, publicly available and in real use - hence in-upstream-engine rather than in-production, since the repo is recording the METHOD's adoption and SGLang is an engine you deploy rather than a feature you enable. Its spec-decode support (EAGLE-3, Medusa) is why pap-eff-eagle-3's throughput claim is an SGLang measurement. TWO MECHANISMS IN ONE RECORD, both relevant to the structured-output and agentic slices: RadixAttention is the prefix-KV-reuse answer for multi-turn agent serving, and the compressed-FSM decoding path is a constrained-decoding implementation that belongs alongside Outlines/XGrammar - a useful third data point because it shows the constraint-mask optimisation is being solved INSIDE engines too, not only in standalone libraries. VENUE NOTE: no peer-reviewed venue verifiable; arXiv comment has no venue, so venue = arxiv-preprint, year = ArXiv v1 (Dec 2023). The 6.4x is against 'state-of-the-art inference systems' at the time of writing, which were vLLM/Orca-generation - a baseline that has since improved substantially, so the figure should not be quoted as a standing advantage.
